title: Domestic violence charge records and heat

headline.headline: The adjusted analysis does not clearly establish more DV-charge records on hotter days.
headline.lead: For each 10°F higher daily maximum, the adjusted daily count was +2.9% (95% confidence interval -1.0% to +7.0%). The main analysis used 6,637 core-DV source IDs across 95 ZIP areas and 1,461 days in 2021–2024.
headline.heatwave: The separate heatwave analysis estimated +16.2% (-6.4% to +44.4%). Heatwave means at least three consecutive May–September days at or above that ZIP’s 90th percentile of May–September daily highs in available 2018–2024 weather. This is an analytical definition, not an official heat alert.

populations.all_source_ids: 136,313 conservative source-file plus identifier groups across every supplied record; not verified unique arrests or people. Descriptive tables can include unresolved-date/locality groups.
populations.core_dv: 12,478 source IDs with an explicit core DV-personal-violence charge (243(e)(1), 273.5, historical 262, or 12022.7(e)). Counts are allegations/records, not convictions or true DV incidence.
populations.broad_dv: 15,161 core or domestic-labeled order IDs; broad includes core. Some order statutes can cover non-DV orders. Generic assault/threat/stalking cannot be assumed DV.
populations.weather_eligible_source_ids: Daily ZIP panel is a narrower population: unique date/ZIP, exclusively ADULT subtype, no recorded warrant subtype, no detention/court category, and valid matched local ZIP weather. core/broad/all in daily.json all use this same eligibility filter.
populations.core: Eligible core-DV source-ID count in this ZIP-day.
populations.broad: Eligible core-or-order source-ID count in this ZIP-day; includes core.
populations.all: All eligible source-ID groups in this ZIP-day, including non-DV. Never the all-source release total.
populations.locality_day: One selected ZIP on one selected calendar day, including zero-qualifying-count cells. Not a person-day or county-day.
populations.source_charge_rows: Charge-row counts include duplicate lines and multiple charges per ID; not unique arrests.
populations.dv_order_source_ids: IDs having an order charge, overlapping core when an ID has both. Broad minus core gives additional order-only IDs.
populations.race: Source-reported broad categories, including ethnicity-style labels. Aggregate counts alone cannot establish disparities in offending or arrest risk.

warnings: 2025 is incomplete: 79 dates have no source rows; January-May has 144 monthly ID appearances. Never interpret absent records as confirmed zero arrests or the annual drop as falling violence.
2018 begins July 1. No 2026 arrest data supplied. All other years also lack agency completeness confirmation.
SHERIFF is an administrative locality label whose use changed sharply in 2024. Recorded locality counts are not complete city crime rates.
37 IDs with conflicting years remain unassigned; 172 have conflicting dates. Do not add date-unresolved groups to individual days.
Weather is modeled outdoor ERA5-Land at ZIP/ZCTA representative points, not observed incident-site or personal exposure. 112 ZIPs share 50 grid cells.
All weather days use fixed UTC-7. During standard time, windows begin 23:00 on the prior local civil date; no exact historical-DST midnight alignment.
Filtered charts show unadjusted descriptive rates. Published adjusted regression estimates are static and do not change under filters.
Neither these associations nor their confidence intervals establish causation, countywide DV incidence, or no effect. Intervals omit data-definition and completeness uncertainty.

model_diagnostics.heatwave_definition: ZIP-specific 90th percentile of May-Sep daily maxima during available 2018-2024; 3+ consecutive May-Sep days at/above threshold; all days in qualifying runs flagged; not official weather alerts
model_diagnostics.all_zero_zip_rule: Drop ZIPs with no outcome in fitted period to avoid divergent fixed effects;retain them in full panel and raw rates
model_diagnostics.multiple_testing: One primary test; all remaining models designated retrospective sensitivity/exploratory. Both unadjusted and Holm-adjusted p-values across all 11 secondary tests are supplied; confidence intervals are individually 95%, not simultaneous. Do not select the strongest test.

classification.ambiguous_related: Other assault/threat/stalking/child or elder abuse/protective-order codes remain unconfirmed without victim relationships.

weather.mean_definition: API daily arithmetic aggregation of hourly modeled 2m air temperature; not (high+low)/2
weather.day_definition: API 24-hour aggregation requested with America/Los_Angeles; response applies a single fixed UTC offset to the whole range, not historical daylight-saving transitions. The saved responses use UTC-7: 07:00 UTC on date through before 07:00 UTC next date. This corresponds to local civil days during daylight time but starts 23:00 on the preceding date during standard time.
weather.coordinates: Census 2024 Gazetteer ZCTA representative internal points, not incident addresses; ZIP-to-ZCTA string matching is approximate

filter_rules.default: 2021-01-01 through 2024-12-31 inclusive, all 112 ZIPs; zero-count rows stay in denominators.
filter_rules.rate_per100_zip_days: 100*sum(selected outcome counts)/number of selected ZIP-day rows, including zeros. Under date/ZIP/temperature filters count every matching row, not only positive records.
filter_rules.weekday_denominator: For weather-panel weekday plots, count matching selected ZIP-days for each weekday. For all-source daily totals, count selected calendar dates for each weekday.
filter_rules.temperature_bands: High <60, 60<=high<70, 70<=high<80, 80<=high<90, 90<=high<100, high>=100°F. Integer fields high10/mean10/low10 require division by 10.
filter_rules.2025: Allow only with prominent incompleteness warning. Show exported-record counts, never call missingness observed zero violence. Keep separate from primary 2021-2024.
filter_rules.model_estimates: Static full designated retrospective sample; never relabel as the filtered ZIP/date estimate.
